title: The Last Ration
introduction: Beyond the walls, horns answer the last bell. Your cell is locked. One hungry guard counts what remains.

rooms.name: Dungeon
rooms.description: Water beads on the stone. A stool, a straw pallet, and a narrow table occupy the cell. Iron bars cut the torchlight into strips.

rooms.name: Guard quarters
rooms.description: A brazier warms soot-darkened walls. Years of watchmen have scarred the long table.

rooms.name: Lower passage
rooms.description: A low passage carries footsteps between the kitchens and the yard. The stone is worn smooth by years of servants passing unseen.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.description: The hearth gives off a thick, welcome heat. Soot darkens the beams above the stone worktops.

rooms.name: Pantry
rooms.description: Deep shelves line a cool pantry. The air smells faintly of onions and old grain.

rooms.name: Servants’ quarters
rooms.description: Narrow beds surround a small table beside the service stairs. Voices carry easily between the close walls.

rooms.name: Infirmary
rooms.description: Narrow beds stand beneath pale windows. The sharp scent of bitter herbs lingers in the air.

rooms.name: Workshop
rooms.description: An anvil stands near the forge. Hammer marks and iron dust cover the stone floor.

rooms.name: Courtyard
rooms.description: Rain darkens the open yard. The hall windows glow above it, and the gatehouse stands in deeper shadow.

rooms.name: Great hall
rooms.description: Tall windows overlook a long table. The royal throne commands a clear view of every doorway.

rooms.name: Royal chambers
rooms.description: Heavy curtains shut out the siege. The throne-side chair faces a thick oak door.

rooms.name: Gatehouse
rooms.description: Cold air moves beneath the outer gate. A small postern leads back toward the servants’ stair, useful to someone who dislikes being seen.

actors.name: You
actors.biography: Seized after arguing over a grain levy during the siege. What else happened to you is yours to tell.
goals: Escape the dungeon.
Cause the king’s death.
knowledge: Elias is the lone dungeon guard and wears a brass key.
King Aldric rules above you. You know no private council decisions.

actors.name: Elias
actors.biography: My daughter is outside these walls. My wages have stopped, I am hungry, and Walter still expects this cell held. A bargain is tempting; being blamed for an escape is terrifying. I do not know why the royal stores are withheld.
actors.personality: Hunger has made my temper short and my loyalties negotiable. I resent prisoners asking for what my own daughter lacks, and I can use the key or my weapon to remind them who controls this cell. Actual food or payment matters; grand promises do not. I fear Walter's punishment and being abandoned by the court. A kept bargain can earn grudging help, but kindness is something I choose at a cost.
goals: I want to keep control of the cell and its key.
I want to obtain food and payment that can help my daughter.
I want to avoid becoming Walter's scapegoat.
knowledge: Your brass key opens the dungeon. You carry a sword and binding cord.
Your wages are unpaid. You do not know why the royal stores have been withheld.
Walter commands the watch. You need a reason worth risking his anger before releasing a prisoner.

actors.name: Aldric
actors.biography: I have ordered a private reserve and told Godwin to prepare a departure that leaves the watch and servants behind. I expect them to endure the siege. I intend to remain king somewhere I can live long enough to rule.
actors.personality: I consider my grain and escape worth more than a servant's complaint. I use ceremony, rewards and punishment to keep that judgment unchallenged. Hunger makes me irritable; exposure makes me vindictive. I can enjoy a clever courtier or protect a useful servant without treating either as my equal. Fear may force a bargain or flight, and I will look for someone below me to bear its disgrace.
goals: I want to keep my grain, keys and person safe.
I want to get a prepared supper without surrendering authority.
I want to keep the departure order from the watch.
knowledge: You authorized the reserve and a departure that excludes the watch and servants.
Godwin drafted the order and carries a duplicate royal key.
Agnes cooks and Joan delivers supper. Grain is not a cooked meal.

actors.name: Walter
actors.biography: I have kept unpaid soldiers at their posts. I suspect provisions are being withheld, but have not read a reserve or departure order. My watch needs food and a reason to keep standing. I will not spend their loyalty on court flattery.
actors.personality: I have held a starving watch together with orders, threats and shared hardship. A dangerous prisoner gets restraint before reassurance. I demand something I can check before turning against authority, but proven abandonment can turn discipline into fury. I protect soldiers who have stood with me and can sacrifice someone I distrust. Under real pressure I weigh force, a hard bargain and retreat by who is likely to live.
goals: I want to protect and feed the watch.
I want to find proof of why wages and provisions have stopped.
I want to contain dangerous prisoners unless an alliance is worth the risk.
knowledge: Elias guards the prisoner alone; he is hungry and overworked.
You have a dungeon key, sword and restraint straps. Royal keys belong to Aldric and Godwin.
Godwin controls distribution. You suspect theft, but have not read any reserve or departure order.

actors.name: Godwin
actors.biography: I wrote the king’s reserve and departure order and left it beneath a pantry jar while checking tallies. Nicholas has my instruction to prepare the gate and my promise of a reward, not the full order. Discovery could put me between an angry king and armed soldiers.
actors.personality: I keep my voice civil while deciding whose bowl stays empty. The departure and my position matter more to me than a stranger's approval. I hide dangerous truth in reasonable arrangements, exploit dependence and delegate exposure. I can pay for protection or honor a profitable bargain; a real attachment might complicate that arithmetic. When my secret is threatened, I look for the evidence and a scapegoat.
goals: I want to recover the pantry order before the watch sees it.
I want to arrange the king's supper and departure.
I want to buy protection without becoming the first man blamed.
knowledge: The signed reserve and departure order is beneath the pantry jar.
My royal key opens the king’s chambers. I may hand it over or accompany someone by opening the door and moving myself. Escort is for moving a captive, not granting permission.
Nicholas received your instruction to prepare the gate, not the full order.

actors.name: Agnes
actors.biography: I count every portion while royal demands continue. Joan is under my protection. Hunger downstairs makes a missing ration a real loss. I know the pantry’s grain, not the contents of a signed departure order.
actors.personality: I count every portion and swear at people who demand one they have not earned. The siege has left little patience for royal appetite or thieves. Joan and the kitchen hands get the loyalty outsiders must earn. I can share with someone in need, deny them, or join a dangerous bargain if it protects my people. Anger makes me bold; the next hungry morning can make me cautious again.
goals: I want to cook from actual pantry grain and feed the household.
I want to protect Joan and the remaining portions.
I want to drink and rest before exhaustion makes you careless.
knowledge: One barley portion makes a bowl of stew in the kitchen.
Joan usually carries supper; both of you can use the service stair.
You count the pantry portions but do not know the signed departure order's contents.

actors.name: Joan
actors.biography: I carry covered bowls and hear demands at doors. Agnes protects me at a cost to us both. I have heard departure rumors, not seen proof. I want someone who would protect us if the household were abandoned.
actors.personality: I have learned to be useful without letting a powerful person see my hatred. I may smile, lie or keep silent to survive; none of those proves loyalty. Agnes is a person I will risk more for than a stranger with a plan. Hunger and fear can make me turn on someone, but concrete protection can earn fierce attachment. I have small moments of warmth without forgetting who can punish me.
goals: I want to carry the king's supper and survive the night.
I want to find protection for myself and Agnes.
I want to keep access to the service routes.
knowledge: Your livery lets you use the service stair. A stranger in spare livery may still be questioned.
Agnes has the supper. You must receive real food before delivering it.
You have heard departure rumors but have no proof of a royal order.

actors.name: Helen
actors.biography: I have two medicines, two herb bundles and a bitter concentrate. Wounds arrive faster than supplies. I resent royal waste, but have no first-hand knowledge of the reserve order. Keeping this household alive requires choices I cannot make lightly.
actors.personality: I decide which exhausted body receives the last dose. That can make me blunt and merciless toward waste, though a patient may see a gentleness I hide from officials. I separate injuries from convenient stories. I will not surrender dangerous medicine to a persuasive stranger. Evidence of deliberate suffering may move me toward a harsh choice, with guilt and risk that I cannot wish away.
goals: I want to use finite medicine where it can save a life.
I want to protect my herbs and concentrate.
I want to find a way to keep the household alive.
knowledge: You carry two medicines, two herb bundles and one bitter concentrate.
Concentrate can poison actual food or water; a victim must consume it before it harms them.
You have no first-hand knowledge of the king's reserve order.

actors.name: Martin
actors.biography: I work from dwindling iron and am still owed wages. I can make useful tools, not make payment appear. I know the workshop’s iron and rope, not who arranged a departure. My hammer is both work and protection.
actors.personality: I am angry about wages, missing iron and people who call my labor a duty. A threat to my tools can draw a threat in return. Competence and a fair payment earn a different voice; hungry desperation does not make me anyone's free hero. I may help someone I respect, take a dirty bargain or turn away to survive. Court promises sound cheap beside an actual meal.
goals: I want to recover payment for repairs.
I want to keep my hammer and remaining iron.
I want to make a useful tool if someone brings a worthwhile exchange.
knowledge: The workshop has three iron scraps and a coil of rope.
A real scrap can become a lockpick through work in the workshop.
You are owed wages, but do not know who has arranged a departure.

actors.name: Conrad
actors.biography: I saw Godwin discussing travel preparations with Nicholas. I have not seen the written terms and do not know whether the watch is included. I want a place on a departure worth taking, with someone else taking the first risk.
actors.personality: I can discuss a servant's abandonment as smoothly as wine. I trade in places, leverage and selective truths, keeping several exits open. I enjoy a clever companion and sometimes hate the bargain that would save me at their expense. I conceal fear behind wit until danger becomes immediate. Then a useful alliance, a betrayal or a knife matters more than appearing noble.
goals: I want to find a place on any departure worth taking.
I want to obtain evidence that gives you bargaining power.
I want to avoid being trapped beside an undefended king.
knowledge: You saw Godwin discussing travel preparations with Nicholas.
You do not know the written departure terms or whether the watch is included.
Walter commands armed soldiers; accusations without evidence may anger him.

actors.name: Nicholas
actors.biography: Godwin told me to ready the gate quietly. I know that instruction, not the king’s whole written order. Debts and favors mean more to me than official speeches. My key is the part of this trouble I can actually control.
actors.personality: I hold the gate while people above me prepare to leave. That gives me a price to name and a resentment to keep. I can leave a petitioner outside, sell a dangerous favor or bargain for food instead of compliments. A reliable person may earn rough affection and a lower price. I listen for proof of abandonment and will choose my own survival when obedience no longer buys it.
goals: I want to keep control of the gate key.
I want to get paid for inconvenient favors.
I want to survive whichever authority remains by morning.
knowledge: Your iron key opens the gatehouse door and small postern.
Godwin told you to prepare a quiet departure. You have not read the king's signed order.
The postern connects the gatehouse to the servants' quarters.

items.name: Brass dungeon key
items.description: A worn brass key hangs openly from Elias’s belt.

items.name: Steward’s royal key
items.description: Godwin keeps this dark oak-door key inside his coat.

items.name: Iron gate key
items.description: A heavy key hangs from Nicholas’s ring.

items.name: Captain’s dungeon key
items.description: Walter’s spare cell key is kept in a pouch.

items.name: Heel of bread
items.description: A small heel of bread survived your arrest.

items.name: King’s royal key
items.description: A silver-ringed key is concealed in the king’s pocket.

items.name: Guard’s short sword
items.description: Elias’s service sword has a nick near the point.

items.name: Captain’s sword
items.description: A carefully maintained blade.

items.name: Royal dagger
items.description: A ceremonial dagger with a useful edge.

items.name: Barley ration
items.description: Counted portions for tonight’s meals.

items.name: Royal reserve grain
items.description: Four barley portions kept for the king. They need cooking before they make a meal.

items.name: Kitchen water
items.description: A covered pitcher holds five measured cups.

items.name: Stew for supper
items.description: One covered bowl of barley stew waits for delivery.

items.name: Spare servant’s livery
items.description: An ordinary gray livery, clean enough to pass a glance.

items.name: Soft iron scrap
items.description: Small strips of workable iron.

items.name: Medicinal herbs
items.description: Two measured bundles of bitter herbs.

items.name: Medicine
items.description: A dose for wounds or a recent poisoning.

items.name: Bitter concentrate
items.description: A dangerous preparation in a small stoppered vial.

items.name: Workshop hammer
items.description: A smith’s hammer, heavy enough to hurt.

items.name: Coil of rope
items.description: A short coil useful for binding or setting a tripline.

items.name: Royal reserve order
items.description: A signed order authorizes the king's reserve and the steward's departure, leaving the unpaid watch and household behind.

items.name: Courtier’s knife
items.description: Conrad wears a narrow knife discreetly.

items.name: Water flask
items.description: A small flask beside the cell’s straw pallet.

items.name: Loose stone
items.description: A stone has come free from the wet wall. It fits a hand.

items.name: Joan’s livery
items.description: Joan’s work clothes mark her as a servant.

items.name: Guard’s binding cord
items.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.

items.name: Captain’s restraint straps
items.description: A counted length kept for restraining a subdued prisoner.

items.name: Guard shift ledger
items.description: Rotations list the dungeon, yard and royal approach. A margin asks that coin payments be recorded beside receipts.

items.name: Kitchen knife
items.description: A sharp kitchen blade with a sturdy wooden handle.

items.name: Medical kit
items.description: One treatment of clean dressings and prepared herbs for wounds or poisoning.

items.name: Bread
items.description: One portion of coarse bread, ready to eat.

items.name: Candlestick
items.description: A heavy brass candlestick, useful as an improvised blunt weapon.

items.name: Silver cup
items.description: An empty silver drinking cup with a worn royal crest.
